questions.prompt: In the fraction 2/7, which number is the denominator?
questions.explanation: The denominator is the bottom number — the 7.
questions.misconception: The top number (2) is the numerator; the denominator sits at the bottom of the fraction.

questions.prompt: What does the denominator 5 tell you in the fraction 2/5?
options: The whole is split into 5 equal parts
Each part is the size of 5
questions.explanation: The denominator 5 names the total equal parts the whole is divided into.
questions.misconception: The numerator 2 is the count you have — the denominator is the total equal parts in the ONE whole.

questions.explanation: More cuts mean smaller pieces — 1/8 is the smallest because the whole is split into the most parts.
questions.misconception: A larger denominator means SMALLER parts, not bigger — 1/8 is half the size of 1/4.

questions.explanation: With the same numerator 2, the larger denominator makes smaller parts — so 2/5 is the smallest.
questions.misconception: With matching numerators, compare only the denominators: a bigger denominator means a smaller fraction, so 2/5 < 2/3.

questions.prompt: Why do you need a COMMON denominator to add fractions like 1/2 + 1/3?
options: So both fractions describe parts of the same size
questions.explanation: Only same-sized parts can be counted together, so both fractions must share a common denominator before adding.
questions.misconception: Adding 1/2 + 1/3 ≠ 2/5 — halves and thirds are different-size parts; a common denominator (sixths) is required first.
